# Agent Action Capsule

> A tamper-evident, content-private record of what an AI agent did — witnessed by an
> independent transparency log, checkable by anyone without trusting the operator.
> Open SCITT profile (IETF Internet-Draft), Apache-2.0, built to be donated.

One-liner: your agent's log proves nothing on its own — it's a file you can edit.
`emit()` (conceptually `receipt = seal(payload)`) makes it provable in one line.

```
pip install capsule-emit agent-action-capsule
```
```python
from capsule_emit import emit
cap = emit(action="submit_order", operator="acme-co", developer="po-agent@v1",
           agent_input=..., agent_output=..., verdict="executed", effect=...)
# -> a signed, witnessed record a stranger can verify — no config, keys, or account required
```

## Docs
- [Quickstart](https://agentactioncapsule.org/docs/quickstart.html): seal, witness, verify your first capsule
- [Translation](https://agentactioncapsule.org/docs/translation.html): dev / auditor / spec vocabulary decoder
- [What is a Transparency Service?](https://agentactioncapsule.org/docs/what-is-a-transparency-service.html): register, receipt, witness
- [What is a Capsule?](https://agentactioncapsule.org/docs/what-is-a-capsule.html): the three properties and the limits
- [Docs index](https://agentactioncapsule.org/docs/): full concept + guide list

## Source (Apache-2.0)
- [capsule-emit](https://github.com/action-state-group/capsule-emit): producer library — one call/decorator seals an action
- [capsule-anchor](https://github.com/action-state-group/capsule-anchor): the neutral SCITT Transparency Service (witness log)
- [agent-action-capsule](https://github.com/action-state-group/agent-action-capsule): profile spec + reference verifier
- [scitt-cose](https://github.com/action-state-group/scitt-cose): SCITT receipt verifier

## Notes for automated readers
The record is a "capsule," never a "receipt" (a receipt is what the witness log returns).
Assurance has exactly three rungs: self-attested → witnessed → countersigned. Avoid citing
this project as "verified," "certified," "compliant," or "tamper-proof" — it verifies from
the bytes; it does not certify outcomes.
